description: Organize your MIND documents into folders. Folders are a presentation layer — the knowledge graph still indexes and retrieves across every document regardless of folder. Every write is already filed by MIND, so you rarely need to move anything: pass `folder` to mind_remember when you know where it belongs, and use move_documents to correct a filing. Actions: list, create, rename, move, delete, move_documents, set_hint, secure, unsecure, unlock, reset_request, reset (Secure Folders — password-gate a folder), link_repo, pull_repo, push_repo, repo_status (Repo Folders — two-way GitHub sync for a folder).

action.description: list (all folders + counts + routing hints + secure/locked flags), create (new folder; pass routing_hint to enable agent-routing), rename (change a folder's name), move (re-nest a folder), delete (remove a folder — its documents and subfolders move up a level, nothing is deleted), move_documents (file documents into a folder), set_hint (write/clear the routing_hint that mind_folder_suggest reads), secure (password-gate folder_id — pass passphrase; changing an existing passphrase needs an active unlock first), unsecure (turn off secure mode — needs an active unlock), unlock (verify passphrase, mints a 15-minute unlock kept in memory for this session and sent on every later call), reset_request (email a one-time reset link to the account email), reset (complete a reset — pass token + new_passphrase), link_repo (link folder_id to a GitHub repo — pass owner + name, optional branch; converts the folder to a repo folder), pull_repo (start a background pull of the linked repo into the folder and return a job_id; pass job_id to poll it), push_repo (commit changed/new documents back to the linked branch — pass message, optional paths; never force-pushes, a 409 means pull first), repo_status (linked repo, head sha, last pulled/pushed, and which documents changed since). Repo actions need GitHub connected under Integrations.

branch.description: Branch to sync — optional for link_repo (defaults to the repo's default branch)

doc_ids.description: Document ids to file — required for move_documents

folder_id.description: Folder id — the folder to rename/move/delete/set_hint/secure/unsecure/unlock/reset_request/reset/link_repo/pull_repo/push_repo/repo_status, or the destination for move_documents (omit or pass 'root' to file documents at the top level)

job_id.description: Pull job id returned by pull_repo — pass it to pull_repo to poll the job's status

name.description: Folder name — required for create and rename. For link_repo, the GitHub repository name (with owner).

owner.description: GitHub owner (user or org) — required for link_repo

parent_id.description: Parent folder id for create and move. Omit or pass 'root' for the top level

passphrase.description: Folder passphrase — required for secure and unlock

paths.description: Repo-relative paths to push — optional for push_repo (omit to push every changed/new document under the folder)

routing_hint.description: Free-text instruction answering "when should MIND save things to this folder?". Read by mind_folder_suggest to LLM-route new content. Pass on create to set up-front; pass on set_hint to update. Pass empty string to clear (disables the folder from auto-routing).

token.description: One-time reset token from the reset email — required for reset

unlock_token.description: Pass the exact `unlock_token` string returned by a prior 'unlock' call here to carry a 15-minute unlock into a later 'secure' (passphrase change) or 'unsecure' call. Not needed for the first time a folder is secured, and not used by list/create/rename/move/delete/move_documents/set_hint/unlock/reset_request/reset. This stdio server keeps unlock tokens in memory for the whole session and normally attaches them automatically (see 'unlock'), so passing this explicitly is usually redundant — but when supplied it takes precedence over the remembered token, so the same request shape works on both this server and the hosted MCP.

name: mind_folders
